root_cause.text: In fib6_add_rt2node(), the code dereferences iter->fib6_nh->fib_nh_gw_family without first checking whether iter->nh is non-NULL, causing an out-of-bounds read when the route was created with RTA_NH_ID because such fib6_info lacks the embedded fib6_nh structure.
root_cause.evidence: The commit message explicitly states: "When IPv6 route is created with RTA_NH_ID, struct fib6_info does not have the trailing struct fib6_nh. The cited commit started to check !iter->fib6_nh->fib_nh_gw_family… If iter->nh is not NULL, rt6_qualify_for_ecmp() returns false anyway. Let's check iter->nh before reading iter->fib6_nh and avoid OOB read." The patch adds the condition `(iter->nh || !iter->fib6_nh->fib_nh_gw_family)` to guard the access.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix missing flag cleanup for routes using nexthop objects by adding a check for iter->nh.
intent_record.what: In fib6_add_rt2node, the condition for clearing RTF_ADDRCONF and RTF_PREFIX_RT flags on iter is extended: previously it required '!iter->fib6_nh->fib_nh_gw_family', now it also triggers when 'iter->nh' is non-NULL.
intent_record.how: At runtime, the code now clears these flags if iter uses a nexthop object (iter->nh is set) regardless of the gateway setting in the individual nexthop, ensuring consistent flag handling for routes using nexthop groups.

grouping_result.intent: Fix missing flag cleanup for routes using nexthop objects by adding a check for iter->nh.

relevance_review.reason: The group directly addresses the vulnerability by adding a check for iter->nh before accessing iter->fib6_nh, preventing the out-of-bounds read when routes use nexthop objects.

candidates.rationale: Dereferences iter->fib6_nh without checking if iter->nh is NULL, causing out-of-bounds read when route has RTA_NH_ID.

vuln_statements.explanation: This statement dereferences iter->fib6_nh->fib_nh_gw_family without first checking whether iter->nh is non-NULL. When the route was created with RTA_NH_ID, the fib6_info does not have an embedded fib6_nh structure, causing an out-of-bounds read.
